label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
**Subject:** Re: Our plan for next year

Dear all,

Kiran, thank you for writing it plainly — that helps more than a polite email would, and you're right about the asking. The agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, and I should have looped you in at that point rather than moving ahead. That one is on me, and I'm sorry.

The decision itself was Appa's, and I want him to know that on the thread rather than in private. It started with him on the phone in August, when Rohan showed him the vegetable patch on the garden camera. He said, "I could grow drumsticks there," and that was the seed of the whole thing. Amma and Appa have been talking it through for weeks. So I'm glad you're happy for them, and I want to say it clearly: I am genuinely thrilled. Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable, and one of the entries reads "Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays." (Amma, the murukku achu is non-negotiable. Divya has made that clear and I have no authority over her.)

On Appa's heart, which is the worry I'd answer most carefully, because you are right to raise it:

You're right that visitors don't get free NHS treatment — that is a real cost and I've budgeted for it. Two things, though. Dr. Prakash has agreed to review Appa in March before they fly, and to do a video consult in July, and he's happy to share his notes with me so we're all working from the same picture rather than different versions. And I've got a travel insurance quote with pre-existing cardiac cover, around £640 each for the six months. The agent says it covers the stent; I'm asking him to confirm that in writing before we buy, so there's no ambiguity at claim time.

Practically as well: the annexe at the back is finished — ground floor, no steps, own shower with grab rail. Leicester Royal is fifteen minutes from the house and I know half the cardiology team. That doesn't replace the insurance or Dr. Prakash, but it does mean nobody here is a stranger to us if anything happens.

Amma — Kiran's point about six months away from your own house and your own people is a fair one, and I want you to hear it without anyone deciding for you. The return ticket is flexible, you can go home whenever you like, and no one will think less of you for it. If you'd rather come in December for a month and come back for the spring, we would love that.

Ganesh Chaturthi: I don't think we have to choose. Appa and Amma could fly Leicester to Pune in September and finish the trip there, so they're with you for the festival and with us for the summer. Or — and this is what I'd like to offer — we would pay for your flights to come to Leicester in August, all of you, so you can see the place before the rains and eat rasam with Paati. Either way works, or both.

Kiran, could we do a family video call this Sunday? 4pm UK, 9.30pm India. Appa, Amma, Divya, Anika and Rohan all on. I'd much rather we heard each other's voices than worked this out in threads.

Love to everyone,
Meera
